summary: The public waiter Supabase client reused the default auth storage key, allowing multiple GoTrue clients in one browser context to contend for the same session.
fix: assigned the client the isolated serveflow-waiter-public-auth storage key

summary: Five deployed PL/pgSQL paths failed static runtime validation because of ambiguous identifiers or an enum type mismatch.
fix: stabilized name resolution, waiter assignment conflict handling, and kitchen activity enum writes in migrations 140-141

summary: Customer feedback photos were globally readable from a public storage bucket.
fix: made the bucket private and restricted object reads and persisted paths to the owning restaurant in migration 142

summary: Staff authentication was stored per tab and could not survive browser restart or restore in a new tab.
fix: superseded by REG-006 because durable shared storage broke concurrent dashboard isolation

summary: Manager pages duplicated subscriptions and did not consistently reload after reconnect, browser wake, or network recovery.
fix: migrated all Manager data surfaces to the shared tenant realtime recovery hook

summary: One durable staff auth key allowed a login in any tab to replace Owner, Manager, Cashier, or Kitchen sessions in every other tab.
fix: assigned every browser tab an isolated sessionStorage-backed Supabase auth namespace

summary: Opening a QR session for Restaurant B deleted Restaurant A QR cart and checkout state from shared localStorage.
fix: scoped active QR markers and cleanup to the current restaurant slug

summary: Waiter offline order queues were shared by every restaurant.
fix: scoped queue storage and synchronization to the authenticated waiter restaurant

summary: Owner AI insights could crash in PostgreSQL formatting with too few arguments.
fix: removed PostgreSQL format calls and deployed typed concatenation in migration 143
